diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then there exists a constant $\zeta > 0$ such that for every $z \in \cS$, one can find a point $y \in \cY$ (possibly depending on $z$) satisfying $\bc(y, z) \leq -\zeta$.

issues.failure_explanation: Negating the conclusion only gives, for each candidate margin, a point z such that every y violates at least one component; the violating component may depend on y and k. It does not yield one fixed j that violates the bound for every y and every k, as asserted in (bc-ineq1). The subsequent scalar-component contradiction therefore does not prove simultaneous strict feasibility of all constraints.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Supply a simultaneous compactness argument, for example by proving that the continuous value function $z\mapsto\min_{y\in\cY}\max_j\bc_j(y,z)$ is strictly negative at every $z\in\cS$ using MFCQ and then uniformly negative on compact $\cS$.
issues.overall_effect: The uniform margin used to bound all SCP multipliers is unproved, so the multiplier bounds and all convergence and complexity results relying transitively on them are unsupported.
issues.title: Invalid quantifier negation in the uniform Slater proof
issues.why_classification: The theorem appears recoverable from the stated hypotheses, but repairing the invalid quantifier interchange requires a new nontrivial simultaneous-feasibility and compactness argument rather than a local algebraic edit.

The standing assumptions do not imply this when $\cX$ is unbounded: for example, a smooth bilinear term can be uniformly Lipschitz in x over compact $\cY$ while $\nabla_y f$ grows without bound in x. issues.failure_explanation: The available oracles compute prox$_p$ and prox$_q$, but the algorithm instead requires exact minimization of $p$ over an added moving ball and exact minimization of $q$ over an intersection of surrogate constraint balls, together with optimal multipliers. For general closed convex $p$ and $q$, neither constrained problem is one evaluation of the corresponding unconstrained proximal operator. No implementation or oracle reduction justifies the claimed counts.
